from mcp.server.fastmcp import FastMCP, Context

mcp = FastMCP("jobs")

@mcp.tool()
async def process(files: list[str], ctx: Context) -> str:
    """Process files and report progress."""
    for i, f in enumerate(files):
        await ctx.info(f"Processing {f}")
        await ctx.report_progress(progress=i + 1, total=len(files))
    return f"Processed {len(files)} files"

import asyncio
from mcp import ClientSession, StdioServerParameters
from mcp.client.stdio import stdio_client

params = StdioServerParameters(command="python", args=["server.py"])

async def main():
    async with stdio_client(params) as (read, write):
        async with ClientSession(read, write) as session:
            await session.initialize()
            tools = await session.list_tools()
            print([t.name for t in tools.tools])
            result = await session.call_tool("add", {"a": 2, "b": 3})
            print(result.content[0].text)

asyncio.run(main())

q.q: Which statement about Model Context Protocol (MCP) is TRUE?

q.h: Revisit Lesson 4 › “Discovering and calling tools”. Study the example below.
q.e: ✓ tools/call params contain the tool name and an arguments object. ✗ “The server sends the initialize request to the client after the first tool call.” — actually: The initialize request must not be part of a batch and comes before any other request except ping. ✗ “Form-mode elicitation is the recommended way to collect passwords and API keys.” — actually: URL-mode elicitation was added in the 2025-11-25 revision for sensitive interactions. ✗ “Once approved, MCP tool definitions can never change.” — actually: Detecting changed tool definitions and re-approving them mitigates rug pulls.
